answer: The guideline (dated 22.10.2026) applies the post-2024 regime: aid is 70 % (80 % until 31.3.2024) of the difference between eligible costs (capped at the maximum housing costs) and the basic deductible. From 1.4.2024 the basic deductible is 0.5 x (T - (667 + 94A + 296L)); the 0.42 x (T - (667 + 111A + 246L)) formula applied 1.1.-31.3.2024 and in 2023, and older years' constants are tabulated. An asset test applies (10,000 EUR for one adult, 20,000 EUR for two or more adults; 20 % of the excess is counted as income; assets of 50,000 EUR or more give no entitlement), and owner-occupied dwellings are excluded from 1.1.2025. So the 80 % / old-formula / owner-occupied version is the superseded one.

answer: Since 1.4.2024 there are three municipality groups (I: Espoo, Helsinki, Kauniainen, Vantaa; II: a named list, 24 municipalities in the 1.1.2025 list versus 30 in the 1.4.2024 list; III: all other municipalities); until 31.3.2024 there were four (Helsinki / Espoo-Kauniainen-Vantaa / named list / others). answer: The guideline is written for case officers ('toimihenkilö', 'kun käsittelet hakemusta') and requires a written decision for granting, rejection, revision, termination and recovery. The only steps it expressly describes as automated are the annual-review letter (sent programmatically) and termination of the benefit 'ohjelmallisesti' (with a decision issued) when the renewal application is not returned in time. It does not say whether new applications or change-based revisions are decided by a caseworker or by automation, nor who signs decisions; it refers to separate pages on decision proposals/decision-making and responsible units.

answer: Only data-retrieval automation is mentioned: Kela receives wage data from the Incomes Register and lease/rent-increase data electronically from landlords participating in the rent-contract query (vuokrasopimuskysely), so customers are not asked for data obtainable from the register or a copy of the lease for those landlords; business/new-property asset data come from a tax-data query; and the annual-review letter is sent programmatically. Registration, missing-attachment reminders and pre-calculation are not described; missing information is requested manually (phone, message service or customer letter) and Kela must request it within 30 days.

answer: The guideline defines the imputed 'minimum income' (= amount of the unemployment general support, formerly labour-market subsidy) and when it is applied: person has not registered as a jobseeker although possibly entitled, income-lessness has not been clarified, or it cannot be shown that the person has no possibility to earn such income (not applied e.g. during studies or childcare). For entrepreneurs without YEL a fixed order applies (Incomes Register wages, start-up grant, unemployment benefit, own estimate, minimum income), and for YEL/MYEL entrepreneurs actual income is used if register or tax data show at least double the YEL/MYEL income. Tax data (latest confirmed taxation) is expressly used for recurring capital gains, share-savings-account yield, dividends and assets. A general rule for resolving discrepancies between declared income and Incomes Register/tax data is not given.

answer: Spouses and close relatives living together are always one household regardless of leases. Cohabitation is judged case by case on an overall assessment where no single factor is decisive (dwelling size/privacy, other reason for sharing, leases and actual rent payment, children, shared housing history, conflicting address data), and it must be examined even if the persons are not registered at the same address. People with separate leases for parts of a dwelling are different households unless they are spouses/cohabitants/close relatives; a joint-liability or joint-termination clause does not merge households; cohabitation ends on moving apart (applicant's own declaration decides for cohabitants moving apart); for a disputed child the VTJ address decides.

answer: The guideline only restates the processing-time guarantee: a decision must be given at the latest on the 30th calendar day from receipt of the application. No actual processing times, statistics or internal service-level targets are given.

answer: The trigger is the landlord's request: if the tenant neglects to pay rent fully or partly for two consecutive months, the allowance can be paid directly to the landlord on the landlord's request without the recipient's consent (YAL 25 § 2 mom.). The recipient is heard before the payment is redirected and gets a decision, which is not appealable; if the recipient later asks for payment to herself, the landlord is heard first.

answer: The guideline gives the substantive rule, not the automation scope: general housing allowance ends from the start of the month when a household member becomes entitled to pensioner's housing allowance (single-person household or a two-person spouse/cohabitant household), even if no pensioner's allowance would actually be payable. Pensions that do not entitle to pensioner's housing allowance and therefore leave YAL in place include lump-sum pensions, abandonment support/pension, part-time pension, partial disability pension, partial early old-age pension, unregistered supplementary pension and partial rehabilitation allowances. Nothing is said about which of these cases are handled by automatic termination or which exclusion rules route a case to a caseworker.

answer: Electronic sources named: the Incomes Register (wages, and since 2021 also benefit and pension payment data, excluding sensitive benefits), the landlord rent-contract query (lease and rent-increase data from participating landlords), a tax-data query (business and agricultural assets, newly formed properties; tax data also used for dividends, capital gains and property values) and the population information system (VTJ addresses). Banks are queried only if the applicant does not supply sufficient or reliable data, insurance/investment companies are a secondary source after the applicant. No separate queries to pension insurers, employers or unemployment funds are described (their payment data come through the Incomes Register), and the guideline does not systematically separate 'routine' from 'on request' or mention data-exchange agreements/§ 46 access decisions.

answer: The guideline says overpayments arise in revision, correction or termination decisions (e.g. a retroactive reducing revision creates an overpayment equal to the difference), and relies on the recipient's duty to report changes and the landlord's duty to report tenancy end/move-out; it does not describe systematic data-matching or landlord-notice detection. Recovery is primarily from the applicant, from adult household members under joint liability if recovery fails, from the landlord under YAL 31 § 4 mom. conditions, or by regress set-off against pensioner's housing allowance. Who decides on waiver is not stated; for recovery from a landlord, mitigation is expressly not considered.
